# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, add, approach, art, asserts (+107 more)

# Assistant — verify documented staff effect (staff-assistant)

## Goal
Confirm that `staff-assistant` (Assistant, management-company) is properly defined — card data, parsed typed field, description text and docs — and that it behaves exactly as documented, by adding or tightening a behavioural test that asserts its documented effect and scope. This card is one of 26 per-card verification children under the parent audit epic `MS-0MW6HEBP80070YND`.

## Documented effect (authoritative: GDD Appendix D.4)

- **Ability:** +2 hand slots
- **Scope:** player hand capacity (street-wide)
- **Backing data:** handSlotsAdded=2
- **Engine consumer:** maxHandSize (WeekStart / AiStrategy)
- **Existing behavioural test file:** `tests/main-street/MainStreetStaffCards.test.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Definition verified.** `staff-assistant` in `src/card-data.csv` carries the documented backing data (handSlotsAdded=2), the `description` text states the same effect at the same magnitude using the ×100 consistency rule, and `docs/game/card-catalog.md` / `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` agree.
2. **Parsed field verified.** The typed `StaffCard` field(s) resolve to the documented value (via `parseStaffEffect` for the `effect` column, or the dedicated column) — asserted in a test.
3. **Behavioural test added or tightened.** `tests/main-street/MainStreetStaffCards.test.ts` (or a new focused test file) contains at least one behavioural test that asserts the documented effect AND its scope (player hand capacity (street-wide)) — not merely that the card can be hired. The test fails if the effect is absent, mis-valued or leaks outside its documented scope.
4. **Card-level verifier covers it.** `verifyStaffCard` (`tests/main-street/cards/definitions/runners.ts`) asserts the same data field, so `unitTestStatus` for `staff-assistant` cannot report `pass` vacuously.
5. **Docs updated.** Code comments and the relevant docs reflect any change made while closing this card; no documentation drift remains for this card.
6. **All tests pass.**

## Key Files

- `src/card-data.csv` — `staff-assistant` row.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — `StaffCard` typed fields.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — `parseStaffEffect` / template rebuild.
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` — effect consumer wiring.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetStaffCards.test.ts` — behavioural test to extend.
- `tests/main-street/cards/definitions/runners.ts` — `verifyStaffCard`.
- `docs/game/card-catalog.md` — card catalog row.
- `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` — GDD Appendix D.4 authoritative design.

## Impact

Players who hire the Assistant can rely on its printed ability (+2 hand slots, scope: player) actually happening.

# Per-card expense breakdowns on competitive Turn Summary seats

## Problem statement

On a competitive closing, each seat's Turn Summary expense rows (Staff wages, Community spaces, Business costs) are category totals only: the tooltip shows the committed figure but cannot list the individual cards that make up each category, because `CompetitiveRoundLedger` / `OwnerRoundLedger` carry no per-card cost detail and `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary` builds expense rows via `buildExpenseRows(seat.ongoingCosts)` which returns category-level sums.

## Users

- **Competitive players** — read the Turn Summary after each closing and need to understand exactly how each expense figure arose (which staff members, which community spaces, which businesses), so the next day's decisions are informed.

### User stories

- _As a competitive player, I want the Staff wages row to list each of my staff cards on its own line with the base cost and any modifiers (e.g. Operations Manager discount), so I can see each member's true salary._
- _As a competitive player, I want the Community spaces and Business costs rows to list each space/business on its own line with its base ongoing cost, so I can see what drove my expenses._
- _As a competitive player, I want the expense tooltips to reconcile to the committed category total, including the street-wide Cost Cutter reduction and available-coins clamp lines, so the breakdown is verifiable._

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Staff wages** tooltip for each competitive seat lists each of that seat's staff cards on its own line, showing the base salary (`card.ongoingCost`) and every named modifier with its signed amount (e.g. `Operations Manager: -50`), computing the member's charged salary via `computeStaffSalaryCost`, then reconciling the list to the committed category total (including the street-wide reduction and available-coins clamp lines where applicable).
2. **Community spaces** and **Business costs** tooltips list each owned space/business on its own line with its base ongoing cost (derived from the owner-filtered `state.streetGrid`), reconciling to the committed category total via the street-wide Cost Cutter reduction and clamp lines.
3. The per-card breakdown for competitive seats uses the same data sources and reconciliation as single-player: derived from the owner's `players[ownerId].staffCards` for staff and the owner-filtered `state.streetGrid` for community spaces and businesses, never invented or synthesized.
4. All new copy is localisable through the existing `t()` / `registerLocale` system with English defaults registered at module load; tooltips remain **presentational** (no state mutation, no RNG), **absent-safe** (a legacy/hand-built ledger with no breakdown degrades to the committed total plus the existing explanatory note), and render the same detail level for single-player and each competitive seat's tab.
5. Deterministic automated tests cover the enhanced expense breakdowns for staff, community spaces, and businesses in competitive mode, added to the existing tooltip test suites and run through the test skill.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Hovering any expense line in the competitive Turn Summary now explains the number behind it — every staff member's base salary and discounts, every community space and business's running cost, and how each category total adds up.

## Constraints

- **Derive from committed state only.** Breakdowns are derived from `players[ownerId].staffCards` (staff) and the owner-filtered `state.streetGrid` (community/business) using the same helpers single-player uses (`computeStaffSalaryCost`, `computeStaffSalaryDiscount`, `getSalaryScopeSkills`, `getSlotOwnerId`). No engine changes.
- **Do not invent attribution.** Where the engine's per-card cost cannot be reproduced from committed state, the tooltip falls back to the committed total with an explanatory note.
- **Existing styling and interaction unchanged.** No tooltip layout, hover/tap behaviour, or `TooltipManager` styling changes.
- **No layout regression.** Multi-line tooltips must fit the existing tooltip width/wrapping; no dialog re-layout.
- **Single-player and competitive parity.** The expense breakdown detail is identical on every tab where the data exists.
- **Tests + docs required.** All tests must pass; full suite must pass.

## Existing state

- **Current competitive expense rows** — `buildExpenseRows(seat.ongoingCosts)` in `MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` returns `TurnSummaryExpenseRow[]` with `{ category, label, coins }` only (no `breakdown`). Called from `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary` for each seat.
- **Single-player expense breakdown** — `expenseLineBreakdown(state, category)` in `MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` derives per-card detail from `state.staffCards` and `state.streetGrid`, returning `{ breakdown?: PLLineBreakdown }` with `items: PLBreakdownItem[]` and optional `streetReduction`.
- **Competitive ongoing costs** — `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts` in `MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` computes per-owner costs: staff from `player.staffCards` (per-player), community/business from `state.streetGrid` filtered by `getSlotOwnerId`. The `OwnerOngoingCosts` interface only carries category-level signed totals.
- **Tooltips** — `MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts` already handles breakdown rendering for single-player; the same `buildExpenseLineTooltip` can render competitive breakdowns if the model threads them through.
- **Tests** — `tests/main-street/turn-summary-tooltips.test.ts` has an existing test asserting competitive expense lines stay category-total only (`line.breakdown === undefined`); this test will need updating.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — new `expenseLineBreakdownForOwner(state, ownerId, category)` (or parameterised variant of `expenseLineBreakdown`), update `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary` to thread breakdowns into expense rows via a per-seat `buildExpenseRowsWithBreakdown`.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — no changes expected; derivation uses existing helpers (`computeStaffSalaryCost`, `getSlotOwnerId`, etc.).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts` — no changes expected; `buildExpenseLineTooltip` already handles breakdown rendering.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-tooltips.test.ts` — add/expand tests for competitive expense breakdowns (staff per-card, community per-card, business per-card, reconciliation with Cost Cutter, absent-safe degradation).

## Related work

- `MS-0MWBCACHZ006RTQ9` — *Full breakdown in tooltips of end of turn dialog* (parent: delivered single-player per-card expense/income/incident/totals detail; competitive expenses deferred to this item).
- `MS-0MVRNVHJ50095N9Y` — *Competitive per-seat expense category rows* (established the `OwnerOngoingCosts` category-level structure this item extends).

## Assumptions & decisions (producer may override)

- **A1 — Derive per-card detail from owner-filtered state.** Staff cards come from `players[ownerId].staffCards` (per-player, not shared `state.staffCards`). Community spaces and businesses come from `state.streetGrid` filtered by `getSlotOwnerId(state, i) === ownerId`. Uses the same helpers as single-player. **Recommended** choice — consistent with how `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts` already attributes costs.
- **A2 — No engine changes.** Derivation is a pure read from committed state; no modifications to `OwnerRoundLedger`, `OwnerOngoingCosts`, or engine computation.
- **A3 — Same reconciliation as single-player.** The breakdown includes the street-wide Cost Cutter reduction as a separate line, and the total reconciles to the committed category total.

## Risks

- *Divergence risk*: re-deriving per-item figures from committed state could drift from what the engine actually deducted. Mitigation: derive only from the engine's own helpers (`computeStaffSalaryCost`, etc.) and include the reconcile-to-committed-total lines so drift is visible in the tooltip itself.
- *Regression risk*: the existing test explicitly asserts no competitive expense breakdowns; updating it must be done deliberately. Mitigation: update the assertion alongside the implementation, keep every existing behaviour.
- *Scope-creep risk*: the producer's request could pull in one-off attribution. Mitigation: explicit scope boundary — expense breakdowns only.

# Main Street renderer/HUD/layout modules have no changed-scope test group

**Headline:** The five most-edited Main Street renderer/HUD/layout modules have no changed-scope group and no convention-mapped test, so their suites only run in the full suite — while a matching group elsewhere can replace the selection entirely; add the missing group (and its config-shape pin) here, and verify the union rule landing in SorraAgents.

## Problem statement

`run_tests.py --scope changed` gives a declared `.pi/test-config.json` group precedence over the file-level selector: when a group matches, its commands replace the selection and selection stops there. On top of that, several frequently-edited Main Street modules have **no** group and **no** convention-mapped test — their tests use kebab-case names that never match the module stem — so a slice touching them either runs an unrelated group's single suite or falls back to the full suite. During `MS-0MWBWKZ1G006IBH2` (Staff Pile) this combination let a knowingly-wrong layout-anchor assertion pass the `finish` gate and be caught only by the dev-push full suite.

Measured on this tree on 2026-11-13 with the installed test skill's `changed_scope_selection` (no tests executed — selection only):

| Changed files | Selection today | Should also run |
|---|---|---|
| `src/layouts/main-street.layout.json`, `src/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts`, `tests/main-street/MainStreetLayoutAnchors.browser.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts` | group `hand-bottom-anchor-browser` → `hand-bottom-anchor.browser.test.ts` **only** | the two changed test files |
| `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStaffPile.ts`, `tests/main-street/staff-pile-renderer.test.ts` | group `webgl-clipping-browser` → `webgl-renderer-clipping.browser.test.ts` **only** | the changed staff-pile renderer test |
| `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` (alone) | full suite — `no matching group and no convention-matched test files` | `hud-tooltips.test.ts` and the other HUD tooltip suites |
| `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` (alone) | full suite — same reason | the formatting suites |
| `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` (alone) | full suite — same reason | the staff skill/buff suites |

Two distinct causes:

1. **Group short-circuit (tooling, not this repo).** `changed_scope_selection()` returns the winning group's commands and never unions the changed test files or the other matching groups. Tracked in SorraAgents — see *Scope split* below.
2. **No group, and no stem match (this repo).** None of the 15 declared groups match `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStaffPile.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`, `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts`, `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` or `src/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts`. The convention mapper compares stems only, so `MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` looks for `MainStreetHudTooltips.test.ts`; the real test is `tests/main-street/hud-tooltips.test.ts`, so nothing maps and the gate pays for the full suite (or, worse, is short-circuited onto an unrelated group).

## Users

- **Developer implementing a Main Street slice** — "When my slice only touches the HUD tooltips renderer, the finish gate should run the HUD tooltip tests, so I find my mistake before the dev-push full suite does (40+ minutes)."
- **Producer reviewing a green `finish` verdict** — "When the gate reports the changed-scope run green, I want confidence that it actually executed the tests covering what changed."
- **Agent implementing the same slice** — relies on the gate as its only fast feedback loop.

## Scope split (duplicate-work triage)

The **tooling half** of the original brief is already tracked in SorraAgents and duplicates must not be re-filed or re-implemented from here:

- `SA-0MWA7OD8O001945I` — *test skill: a matched changed-scope group silently drops other changed test files* (open, **high**, `plan_complete`). ACs already pin the union-or-fail-closed rule plus tests (`group path + changed test file outside it` → both emitted; group-only match unchanged).
- `SA-0MVEJIHIG003WTH9` — *Changed-scope gate: run the union of all matching test groups (fix single-group pick) and align selectors* (open, medium, `idea`).

Related **completed** work, for context only:

- `MS-0MVZJ3175002WZO2` (v0.1.24) fixed the *scoring* of the group pick: most-changed-files wins, fewest-commands breaks ties. It did **not** add the union, so the changed-test-file skip survived.
- `MS-0MW0VMTSB004CHYH` raised exactly this skip; closed as a duplicate of `MS-0MVZJ3175002WZO2` without its union AC being implemented.

This item is therefore **narrowed to the tce-side gap**: declare group coverage for the ungrouped modules and layout fixtures, keep the config-shape guard in step, record verification of the evidence slices, and re-verify the union case once `SA-0MWA7OD8O001945I` ships.

Requirement mapping (so nothing is silently dropped):

| Original requirement | Disposition |
|---|---|
| “Union, don't replace — also run the changed test files” | **Delegated** to `SA-0MWA7OD8O001945I` (high, open); this item verifies it (AC4). |
| “Also run the convention-mapped tests for changed sources” | **Delegated** to `SA-0MVEJIHIG003WTH9` (medium, open). |
| “Add or extend groups for the renderer/HUD/layout modules” | **Kept here** (AC1, AC2). |
| “Add a regression test for the union rule” | **Delegated** to `SA-0MWA7OD8O001945I` ACs 2–4 (the tests live with the code); this item records the tce-tree verification (AC3, AC4). |

## Acceptance Criteria

- A change touching any of `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStaffPile.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`, `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts`, `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts`, `src/layouts/main-street.layout.json` or `src/layouts/main-street-tutorial.layout.json` selects a declared `.pi/test-config.json` group (not the full suite), and that group's commands include that module's own test suites.
- `tests/tooling/test-config-timeout-guard.ts` `EXPECTED_GROUP_NAMES` is updated in the same change, so the config-shape guard passes and the two-file rule (`MS-0MVZGAEF6004Q8XD`) is honoured.
- The layout evidence slice (`src/layouts/main-street.layout.json` + `src/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` + `tests/main-street/MainStreetLayoutAnchors.browser.test.ts` + `tests/main-street/tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts`) selects a command set that executes both changed test files; the `changed_scope_selection` output is captured verbatim in a work-item comment.
- After `SA-0MWA7OD8O001945I` ships (recorded as *blocked-by*), a re-run of the renderer evidence slice (`src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` + `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStaffPile.ts` + `tests/main-street/staff-pile-renderer.test.ts`) includes `tests/main-street/staff-pile-renderer.test.ts`, captured verbatim in the same comment thread.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — in particular the changed-scope group table and group inventory in `docs/dev/testing.md`, which currently documents `webgl-clipping-browser` as the outcome for `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts`.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A developer editing the staff-pile, HUD tooltips, formatting, staff-buff or layout modules gets those modules' own tests executed by the changed-scope gate instead of an unrelated single suite or the full 40-minute suite, so a false green can no longer reach the dev-push gate unnoticed.

## Constraints

- **Repository boundary:** `.pi/test-config.json` and `tests/tooling/` are agent infrastructure. This work item is the explicit authorisation for the change (it exists so the config is edited deliberately, not as a side effect of a feature slice) — per the global coding discipline on infrastructure directories.
- **No `run_tests.py` copy here.** The union change belongs in SorraAgents (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`). This repo carries no copy of the skill; do not vendor one.
- **Two-file rule:** adding a group requires the config **and** the `EXPECTED_GROUP_NAMES` pin; forgetting the pin fails `tests/tooling/test-config-timeout-guard.test.ts`.
- **Path patterns** use `fnmatch.fnmatchcase`: `src/layouts/**` covers nested layout files, but module paths need exact file entries (there is no wildcard that matches a whole `src/scenes/MainStreet*` prefix reliably without over-matching unrelated scenes).
- **Group commands** must be runnable as declared against this repo's `unit` / `browser` vitest projects; a group command must never be `npm test` (that is the full suite).
- **Verification is selection-only.** AC3/AC4 are satisfied by capturing `changed_scope_selection(...)` output (a Python import of the runner, which executes **no** suite). Never invoke `vitest`/`npm test` directly to prove it — agent-initiated test runs go through `/skill:test`.
- **Group paths are selection hints, not exhaustive.** A group's `paths` list must not claim a file another group legitimately owns unless the overlap is intended — `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` already appears in `main-street-overlay-dialogs`, `webgl-clipping-browser` and `competitive-turn-summary`, and overlap is what makes the pick ambiguous while the union is pending.

## Existing state

- `.pi/test-config.json` declares 15 groups; none matches the five modules above, and no group's `paths` covers `src/layouts/**` generically (the two current layout files are listed literally under `hand-bottom-anchor-browser`).
- `select_group_from_changed_files()` scores groups by changed-file count with a fewest-commands tie-break (v0.1.24 / `MS-0MVZJ3175002WZO2`); `changed_scope_selection()` still returns on the first group match, so the file-level selector never runs alongside it.
- The convention mapper (`map_changed_to_tests`) matches exact stems only; kebab-case test names (the dominant convention under `tests/main-street/`) never match a PascalCase module.
- `tests/tooling/test-config-timeout-guard.ts` pins `EXPECTED_GROUP_NAMES` and the three-command `suiteCommands` shape.
- `docs/dev/testing.md` § *Changed scope: groups and vitest files are selectable* documents the current mapping with a table whose `MainStreetScene.ts` row says `webgl-clipping-browser` wins.
- Candidate tests per module (all exist today): staff pile — `staff-pile-renderer.test.ts`, `staff-pile.test.ts`, `staff-underlay-rendering.browser.test.ts`; HUD tooltips — `hud-tooltips.test.ts`, `ongoing-cost-tooltips.test.ts`, `staff-skill-tooltip.test.ts`, `sold-card-tooltip.test.ts`; formatting — `card-currency-formatting.test.ts`, `staff-underlay-formatting.test.ts`; staff buffs — `staff-skill-buffs.test.ts`, `staff-skill-buff-wiring.test.ts`, `staff-skill-scope-gate.test.ts`; layout — `MainStreetLayoutAnchors.browser.test.ts`, `tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts`, `layout-adapter.test.ts`, `hud-anchor-source-contract.test.ts`, `screen-layout-mapping.test.ts`.

## Desired change

- **Declare group coverage** in `.pi/test-config.json` for the five ungrouped modules and both layout fixtures. One new group is preferred over five (see Assumptions): a single `main-street-renderer-hud-layout` group with one `unit` command and one `browser` command, whose `paths` list the seven files exactly, plus `src/layouts/**` (so a new layout fixture is covered without a further config change), **and the two layout test files** (`tests/main-street/MainStreetLayoutAnchors.browser.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts`). The two test files are required to satisfy AC3 before the union ships: without them the new group ties `hand-bottom-anchor-browser` on changed-file count for the four-file layout evidence slice (two matching sources each) and loses the fewest-commands tie-break (two commands vs one), so only `hand-bottom-anchor.browser.test.ts` runs. With them the new group matches four changed files and wins, and its commands must run both changed test files.
- **Update the pin** with the new group name in `tests/tooling/test-config-timeout-guard.ts`.
- **Record verification** by running `changed_scope_selection` for each evidence change set (selection only — no test execution) and pasting the output into a work-item comment; repeat the renderer slice once `SA-0MWA7OD8O001945I` ships.
- **Update the docs** — `docs/dev/testing.md`: refresh the changed-scope selection table, list the new group in the group inventory, and state that the union of group + file-level selection is pending `SA-0MWA7OD8O001945I`. Also refresh the stale “fourteen named groups” wording to “fifteen” in `tests/tooling/test-config-timeout-guard.ts` (`structuralProblems` docstring) and the `tests/tooling/test-config-timeout-guard.test.ts` test title (AC5 “code comments”).

**Key Files:**

- `.pi/test-config.json` — add the group: `commands` (one `npx vitest run --project unit …`, one `npx vitest run --project browser …`) and `paths` (the five modules, both layout JSONs, `src/layouts/**`).
- `tests/tooling/test-config-timeout-guard.ts` — add the group name to `EXPECTED_GROUP_NAMES`.
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — changed-scope selection table + group inventory + union-status note.
- `tests/main-street/staff-pile-renderer.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/hud-tooltips.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/card-currency-formatting.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/staff-skill-buffs.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/MainStreetLayoutAnchors.browser.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts` — the suites the new group must run (referenced by the group's `commands`; not modified by this item).
- *(SorraAgents, out of this repo)* `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — the union fix; blocked-by `SA-0MWA7OD8O001945I`.

## Related work

- `SA-0MWA7OD8O001945I` — *test skill: a matched changed-scope group silently drops other changed test files* (open, high) — supplies the union rule this item verifies; **blocks AC4**.
- `SA-0MVEJIHIG003WTH9` — *Changed-scope gate: run the union of all matching test groups and align selectors* (open, medium) — broader union scope, same tooling.
- `MS-0MVZJ3175002WZO2` — completed (v0.1.24): group scoring changed to most-changed-files.
- `MS-0MW0VMTSB004CHYH` — completed as duplicate of the above; its union AC was never implemented (the gap this item inherits for verification).
- `MS-0MWBWKZ1G006IBH2` (Staff Pile) — discovered-from: the slice whose wrong anchor assertion passed the gate.
- `MS-0MWC7NU7W006ZI3X`, `MS-0MWC7Z6OF008J0PP` — the sibling layout/renderer slices whose gate runs under-selected.
- `MS-0MVZGAEF6004Q8XD` — the two-file group/pin rule enforced by `tests/tooling/test-config-timeout-guard.test.ts`.

`/skill:find-related` report (`MS-0MWCL3W0O0016P9K`, automated) also surfaced `MS-0MUML5X1L008LT8Z` (Physiotherapist rename) and `MS-0MUOSUN3O003MA1B` (Investor staff ability tests) — keyword false positives on “staff”/“add”/“tests”, not related. Its repository file matches (`core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`, `core/AGENTS.md`) are generic keyword matches, not documentation that needs updating; the doc surface for this change is `docs/dev/testing.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — one combined group, not five.** A single `main-street-renderer-hud-layout` group (2 commands) covers the modules with the least config churn and one pin edit. Five per-module groups would give finer targeting but multiply the pin edits and the tie-break ambiguity while the union is pending. Trade-off: a staff-buff-only change runs the HUD/formatting tests too — acceptable at these suite sizes.
- **Assumption — tooling stays in SorraAgents.** This item verifies the union rather than re-implementing it, per duplicate-work triage. If the producer prefers the tce item to drive the tooling fix end-to-end, the union implementation moves back into scope and `SA-0MWA7OD8O001945I` should be closed into this item instead.
- **Risk — the renderer-slice AC is coupled to an open SorraAgents bug.** Its completion may wait on `SA-0MWA7OD8O001945I`; the dependency is recorded so the item is visibly blocked rather than silently green.
- **Risk — over-broad `paths`.** Adding `src/layouts/**` is safe (fixtures only), but claiming shared scene files would deepen the existing three-way overlap on `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts`; this item does not do that.
- **Scope-creep candidate (not in scope):** teaching the convention mapper kebab-case stem aliases (`MainStreetHudTooltips` → `hud-tooltips.test.ts`) would remove the need for many groups at all — a SorraAgents tooling change; record as a follow-up rather than widening this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **No clarifying questions were required.** The seed description already stated the problem, the desired change and the evidence. Research performed instead: (a) read `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (`changed_scope_selection`, `select_group_from_changed_files`, `map_changed_to_tests`) in both the installed skills tree and the SorraAgents source — the two copies are identical and still short-circuit on the first matching group; (b) executed `changed_scope_selection` read-only against this tree for five change sets to measure the actual selections recorded in the Problem statement; (c) ran `wl search` for duplicates and found the two open SorraAgents items that own the tooling half; (d) inspected `.pi/test-config.json`, `tests/tooling/test-config-timeout-guard.{ts,test.ts}` and `docs/dev/testing.md` to confirm the two-file pin rule and the doc surface that needs updating.

# Staff go to business or management company

## Problem statement

Hiring a **business staff** card (e.g. the Delivery Driver, `staff-delivery`) from the general market row does not set `employedAtSlot`, so the two-type model's runtime test (`isBusinessStaffCard` = "has an `employedAtSlot`") classifies the member as **management-company staff**. The member then appears in the management-company roster and Staff Pile, its business-scope effect is inert, its salary is still charged, and there is no way to correct it — the roster offers only *Lay off*, never *Assign to a business*. The player reported exactly this: a hired Delivery Driver "went to the management company" even though its card type is *Business*, and clicking it offered no way to assign it to an appropriate business.

**Chosen model (producer decisions Q1/Q2/Q3).** Business-staff cards are hired **unassigned** into the player's staff pool (the Staff Pile) — there is **no** hire-time destination step; the member receives no business-scope benefits until it is employed, while its salary costs remain. The player assigns an unassigned business-staff member to a business afterwards by clicking it / its roster row (*Assign to business*). The docs that currently promise hire-time placement are updated to describe this assign-later model. Roster and Staff-Pile classification is corrected so unassigned business staff are never shown as management-company staff, and the single-player AI/Monte-Carlo hire path places business staff so balance runs stop silently wasting hires.

## Users

- **Human player (single-player)** — hires a business-staff card from the market row; the member joins the staff pool unassigned and is assigned by the player via the staff surface.
  - As a player, when I hire a Delivery Driver I want to click it afterwards and assign it to one of my Food/Commerce businesses, so that its adjacency purchase discount actually applies.
  - As a player, when an unassigned business-staff member has no matching business yet, I want to see it labelled as *unassigned business staff* (not management company), with costs and benefits behaving accordingly, so I know I must either build a matching business or lay the member off.
- **Human player (competitive)** — the same flow, restricted to the businesses their seat owns.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Business-staff hire is unchanged and unassigned is first-class. Hiring a business-staff card (`staffCardScope(card) === 'business'`) from the general market row joins the player's staff pool with **no** `employedAtSlot` and **no** hire-time destination step (Q1-B). An unassigned business-staff member receives no business-scope benefits while its salary is still charged (Q2-B); management-company staff hire is unchanged.
- *Assign to business* affordance. From the staff-management surface (the roster overlay opened from the Staff Pile / a member click), an unassigned business-staff member offers an *Assign to business* action; the player picks a destination that satisfies the existing placement predicate (`canPlaceStaffOnBusiness`: business-type match via `staffMatchesBusiness`, free employment slot via `hasFreeEmploymentSlot`, competitive ownership via `canActiveSeatActOnSlot`). The assignment is executed through `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` — initial placement of an unassigned member stays action-free, a later move of an employed member stays 1 action — and is undoable and logged.
- No legal destination is handled gracefully. When no business the acting seat may employ at matches the member's `allowedBusinessTypes` with a free slot, the member simply remains unassigned (Q2-B): the assign action reports the reason (e.g. "no matching business with a free employment slot") and spends nothing; the member keeps appearing as unassigned business staff until a legal destination exists or it is laid off.
- Roster and type surfaces classify by card type (Q3-A). The management-company roster and Staff Pile list management-company staff only; unassigned business staff are surfaced as an explicit *unassigned business staff* group with the assign affordance and are never presented as management-company staff; employed business staff appear on their business (Manage Card) as today. Effect semantics keyed on `employedAtSlot` are unchanged.
- Lay-off stays available for unassigned business staff. Dismissal of an unassigned business-staff member works from the staff surface with the same quoted cost (one turn's salary + the salary-scaled reputation cost) as other doors.
- Single-player AI / Monte-Carlo hires place business staff (Q3-A). In AI-driven play (Monte Carlo / auto-play), a business-staff hire places the member at a legal destination business as part of the hire; when no legal destination exists the hire action is not taken, so an AI hire is never silently inert. The competitive AI remains staff-free (unchanged).
- Deterministic automated tests cover the matrix: business-staff hire → unassigned for the human player; the assign affordance's legality matrix (type match / no match / no free slot / opponent-owned destination in competitive / no owned business at all); assign is action-free on initial placement and 1 action on relocation; undo/redo and save/load round-trips; roster and Staff-Pile classification (management-company vs unassigned business staff); AI hire-and-place and AI skip-when-no-destination; management-company hire unchanged — seeded and run through the test skill.
- Documentation updated (Q1-B: "update GDD if necessary"). The hire-flow wording in `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/game/card-catalog.md` and `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (D.4) is updated to the assign-later model (currently they promise "hiring business staff chooses the destination business"); code comments, JSDoc, README and any relevant wiki/docs entries are updated too.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player who hires a business-staff card (such as the Delivery Driver) can click the member afterwards and assign it to the business it works at, so the hire actually does what the card promises — until then it is honestly labelled *unassigned business staff* with its costs, rather than masquerading as a management-company employee.

## Constraints

- **One placement predicate.** Destination legality must reuse `canPlaceStaffOnBusiness` (and therefore `staffMatchesBusiness`, `hasFreeEmploymentSlot`, `canActiveSeatActOnSlot`). Do not add a second business-type or ownership check.
- **No hire-time placement step.** Per Q1-B the market-row hire flow is unchanged; the fix is the assign affordance and the classification/doc corrections, not a `placing-staff` phase at hire.
- **Effect semantics stay keyed on `employedAtSlot`.** An unassigned business-staff member's business-scope skills remain inert (the existing scope gate); classification changes affect *display surfaces and AI behaviour*, not buff resolution.
- **Action economy unchanged.** Hire is 1 action; assigning an unassigned member (initial placement) is free; relocating an employed member stays 1 action (`isStaffRelocation`); management-company staff are never placed or relocated.
- **Determinism preserved.** AI/enumeration and applicant-resolution changes must not add or reorder `state.rng` draws in a way that changes seeded outcomes (Monte Carlo baselines may shift only as the intended Q3-A consequence, and must stay seeded/deterministic).
- **Single-player untouched where it should be.** The competitive ownership gate stays a no-op without `ownerTaggedGrid`; existing single-player behaviour passes.
- **No new scope.** Staff salaries, the two-type effect model, the applicant flow and the AI's staff-free competitive strategy are unchanged; extra opportunities (e.g. rebalancing staff salaries) are recorded as linked work items, not folded in here.
- **Backward-compatible saves.** Loads must tolerate older saves that contain unassigned business staff.

## Existing state

- **Hire path never places.** `purchaseStaffCard` (`src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts:1061`) deducts coins, removes the row card and pushes `{ ...card }` into `state.staffCards` (`:1085`) with **no** `employedAtSlot`; `hireStaffCard` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:904`) simply delegates to it. `canPurchaseStaff` (`src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts:1043`) only checks presence and coins — never business availability (this is now the chosen behaviour for the player, per Q2-B).
- **UI hires immediately.** `onStaffCardClick` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts:785`) validates with `canPurchaseStaff` and executes `hireStaffCardCommand` (`:827`) with no destination step — retained as-is under Q1-B.
- **The engine already knows the card is business staff.** `canPlaceStaffOnBusiness` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:996`) gates on `staffCardScope(member) === 'management-company'` (`:1014`), and `staffCardScope` (`src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts:147`) falls back to the template marker for an unplaced card — so an unplaced Delivery Driver is *business* staff to the engine, and `placeStaffOnBusiness` can already place it.
- **The roster uses a different test.** `isBusinessStaffCard` (`src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts:248`) is `employedAtSlot !== undefined`, so an unplaced Delivery Driver is *management-company* staff to every roster/tooltip surface: `buildCompanyRoster` (`src/MainStreetRoster.ts:93`), `selectManagementCompanyStaff` (`src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts:262`) and `buildStaffPileTooltip` (`src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts:701`). That is the visible contradiction ("listed as a business staff member" but sitting in the management company).
- **Effects are inert, salary is not.** Business-scope buffs resolve from `business.employedStaff` (`src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts:74`, `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts`), so an unplaced member contributes nothing, while `applyStaffOngoingCosts` still charges its salary — the behaviour the producer confirmed as intended (Q2-B).
- **No assign door today.** `showCompanyRosterDialog` (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:1906`) offers only [Confirm lay-off]; business rows appear only in the Manage Card once the member is already employed (`buildBusinessStaffRows`, `src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts:74`); `canMoveStaffOnBusiness` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:1091`) rejects an unplaced member (`employedAtSlot == null`) and `buildMoveStaffAffordance` (`src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts:632`) therefore never offers it. `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:922`) is the correct action-free initial-placement command but has **no live UI caller**.
- **Docs promise the superseded model.** `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md:509` and `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md:544` state that hiring business staff "also chooses the destination business — its initial placement is free and part of the hire action"; under Q1-B this wording is updated to the assign-later model (in scope).
- **Single-player AI hires without placing.** `enumerateLegalActions` (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts:837-860`) offers `hire-staff` for any affordable, not-already-employed staff card, with no placement step, so a Monte-Carlo AI hire of business staff is inert (Q3-A fixes this).
- **Tests.** `tests/main-street/staff-two-type-redesign.test.ts` asserts that hiring *management-company* staff never assigns a destination; `staff-general-market-purchase.test.ts` covers the coin/hand mechanics only; no test covers the assign-affordance flow or roster classification of unassigned business staff.

## Desired change

1. Keep the market-row hire exactly as it is (Q1-B): business staff join unassigned; no destination step.
2. Add the *Assign to business* interaction for unassigned business-staff members: an affordance on the staff surface (roster overlay / member click), a destination picker derived from `canPlaceStaffOnBusiness`, executed via `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` (action-free initial placement), undoable and logged.
3. ## Problem statement

The competitive HUD scoreboard draws each seat's row label in that seat's raw persisted colour (`row.colour ?? NEUTRAL_ROW_COLOUR`). The colour-blind-safe palette deliberately includes the Okabe–Ito black (`#000000`), so a seat assigned that hue renders an unreadable label on the dark HUD bar. The same defect was already fixed for the Turn Summary tab strip (MS-0MWBWRITL0089GGJ) by the shared `ensureReadableSeatColour()` helper; the HUD simply never adopted it.

## Users

- **Competitive player** — can read every rival's coin/reputation/score row on the scoreboard regardless of which palette colour a seat was dealt.
- **Single-player player** — unaffected; no roster means no per-seat rows are drawn.

Example user story:

- As a competitive player, when a seat is dealt the palette's black, I can still read that seat's scoreboard row so I can track their totals.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A competitive HUD scoreboard row whose seat colour falls below WCAG AA contrast against the HUD background is lightened toward white via `ensureReadableSeatColour()`, so the row label is always readable.
- The HUD passes the actual HUD bar background as the contrast backdrop (not merely the dialog-panel default), so the check matches the surface the text sits on.
- A seat colour that already clears the ratio is drawn unchanged (the exact caller string), preserving seat identity.
- The existing neutral fallback (`NEUTRAL_ROW_COLOUR`, used only for a malformed/absent seat colour) is preserved.
- Unit/browser coverage pins the black-seat case on the HUD: a seat dealt `#000000` renders a label that clears WCAG AA against the HUD background, while a legible seat keeps its exact hue.
- All existing tests pass.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

No competitive player loses a scoreboard row to an unreadable seat colour.

## Constraints

- Presentation-only: resolve the text colour for rendering; do not mutate persisted `PlayerRecord.colour`, consume RNG, or add a persisted field.
- Reuse, don't fork: `ensureReadableSeatColour()` and its colour maths in `src/MainStreetSeatColours.ts` remain the single source of legibility truth (same helper as the Turn Summary tab strip).
- UK English spelling in comments, tests and docs.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererCompetitiveHud.ts` — `renderCompetitiveScoreboard()` builds rows from `buildCompetitiveScoreboard()` and sets the Phaser text `color` to `row.colour ?? NEUTRAL_ROW_COLOUR` (currently `#ffffff`) with no contrast adjustment.
- `src/MainStreetSeatColours.ts` — already exports `ensureReadableSeatColour(seatColour, backgroundHex = DIALOG_PANEL_BACKGROUND, minContrast = MIN_SEAT_TEXT_CONTRAST)`, plus `parseHexColour`, `contrastRatio`, `mixTowardWhite`, `toHexColour`. It lightens a too-dark colour toward white in 20 steps until it clears WCAG AA (4.5:1); a colour that already clears the ratio is returned unchanged.
- The HUD bar is drawn as `s.add.rectangle(hudLeft, hudY, hudWidth, HUD_BAR_HEIGHT_PX, PANEL_FILL, PANEL_FILL_ALPHA)` in `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts`, where `PANEL_FILL = 0x1a1408` and `PANEL_FILL_ALPHA = 0.85` (a very dark brown, not pure black). The row text is drawn above the bar at `hudY - HUD_BAR_HEIGHT_PX / 2 - HUD_SEAT_ROW_OFFSET_PX`.
- Existing test file `tests/main-street/competitive-hud-colour.test.ts` asserts each row is drawn in its persisted colour; that assertion must be reconciled with the new legibility rule (legible seats unchanged, illegible seats lightened).

## Desired change

1. In `renderCompetitiveScoreboard()`, resolve the row text colour through `ensureReadableSeatColour(row.colour ?? NEUTRAL_ROW_COLOUR, <HUD bar background>)` instead of using the raw seat colour.
2. Pass the real HUD bar background (the `PANEL_FILL` hex, e.g. `#1a1408`) as the backdrop argument so the contrast threshold matches the drawn surface.
3. Extend `tests/main-street/competitive-hud-colour.test.ts` with a black-seat legibility case and keep the "legible seat keeps its exact hue" assertion.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererCompetitiveHud.ts` — resolve the row text colour through `ensureReadableSeatColour()`
- `src/MainStreetSeatColours.ts` — existing shared helper (no change expected; reference only)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — `PANEL_FILL` / `PANEL_FILL_ALPHA` HUD bar background constants
- `tests/main-street/competitive-hud-colour.test.ts` — extend with the legibility case

## Related work

- **MS-0MWBWRITL0089GGJ** — Turn summary shows a true summary tab (completed): discovered-from parent; its audit-rejection fix introduced `ensureReadableSeatColour()` for the tab strip and filed this HUD follow-up.
- Related docs: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (competitive HUD / scoreboard sections).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Backdrop choice (low).** Passing the real HUD bar colour (`#1a1408`) rather than the dialog default slightly changes which hues are lightened. Mitigation: pass the HUD constant and pin the black-seat case in tests.
- **Test reconciliation (low).** The existing "renders each seat in its persisted colour" test will now be false for an illegible hue. Mitigation: keep the exact-hue assertion for legible seats and add an explicit lightened-hue assertion for black.
- **Scope creep.** Any broader seat-colour legibility audit (e.g. placed-card borders) is out of scope and becomes a linked work item.
- **Assumption.** The black palette entry is the only palette colour that fails AA against the HUD bar; the helper handles any future addition generically.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

No producer interview was required: the seed context (filed as `discovered-from:MS-0MWBWRITL0089GGJ`), the existing shared helper and the referenced renderer/tests were sufficient to draft the brief. The one implementation nuance worth recording was resolved by repo inspection:

- Q: Which background should `ensureReadableSeatColour()` compare against on the HUD? — Answer (agent, researched): the **HUD bar fill**, `PANEL_FILL = 0x1a1408` at `PANEL_FILL_ALPHA = 0.85` (`src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts`, drawn in `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts`), not merely the dialog-panel default `DIALOG_PANEL_BACKGROUND = '#000000'`. Recorded in the ACs and Desired change. Source: repo inspection of `MainStreetRendererHud.ts` / `MainStreetConstants.ts` / `MainStreetSeatColours.ts`.
- Q: Does the fix require changing the shared helper? — Answer (agent, researched): no; `ensureReadableSeatColour()` already supports an explicit `backgroundHex`, so this is a call-site change plus tests. Source: `src/MainStreetSeatColours.ts`.

# Model: owner-filtered expense breakdown derivation

## Goal

Generalise the single-player per-card expense breakdown so it can be derived for
one owner, giving competitive seats the same per-card detail from the seat's own
committed state.

Parent: `MS-0MWBZDVCH008P8X5` — *Per-card expense breakdowns on competitive Turn Summary seats*.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `expenseLineBreakdownForOwner(state, ownerId, category)` in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`; make `expenseLineBreakdown(state,
  category)` delegate to it so single-player output is unchanged.
- Staff source: the owner's `players[ownerId].staffCards` when a roster exists,
  else the shared `state.staffCards` (single-player / hand-built states).
- Community-space and business source: `state.streetGrid` filtered by
  `getSlotOwnerId(state, i) === ownerId`, sold slots excluded.
- Street reduction: the owner's `getStreetScopeSkills(owner.staffCards)` for
  staff and `getEmployedSpecializationSkills(state)` for community/business,
  mirroring `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts` (`hostReduction`).
- Keep the existing item shape (`name`, `coins`, `base`, `modifiers`) and the
  invariant `base + sum(modifiers) === coins`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `expenseLineBreakdownForOwner(state, ownerId, category)` derives per-card expense breakdown items for one owner, and the existing single-player `expenseLineBreakdown(state, category)` delegates to it so single-player breakdown output is unchanged.
- Staff breakdown items for a competitive seat come from that owner's `players[ownerId].staffCards`, with `coins` from `computeStaffSalaryCost(getSalaryScopeSkills(card), card.ongoingCost)`, `base` = `-card.ongoingCost` and every named modifier (e.g. Operations Manager) with its signed amount.
- Community spaces and business costs breakdown items list each owned space/business on its own line with its base ongoing cost, derived from the owner-filtered `state.streetGrid` via `getSlotOwnerId`, excluding sold slots and synthesising no modifiers.
- The street-wide reduction is computed from the same skill set the engine uses per category: the owner's `getStreetScopeSkills(players[ownerId].staffCards)` for staff and `getEmployedSpecializationSkills(state)` for community spaces and businesses.
- Absent-safe: an unknown owner, a roster-less or hand-built state, or an empty source yields no breakdown (`{}`) rather than an empty item list or a throw.
- The per-card breakdown for competitive seats uses the same data sources and reconciliation as single-player: derived from the owner's `players[ownerId].staffCards` for staff and the owner-filtered `state.streetGrid` for community spaces and businesses, never invented or synthesised.
- Presentational and pure: deriving a breakdown mutates no state, consumes no RNG and needs no engine change.

## Impact

A single pure helper can now explain any owner's expense category from that owner's own committed cards, which is what the competitive panel needs.

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — `expenseLineBreakdown`, new `expenseLineBreakdownForOwner`, `streetReduction`
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — `computeStaffSalaryCost`, `computeStaffSalaryDiscount`, `getSalaryScopeSkills`, `getStreetScopeSkills`, `getEmployedSpecializationSkills` (read-only reuse)
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts` — `getSlotOwnerId` (read-only reuse)

# Business expense breakdown ignores the Bookkeeper per-business reduction

## Goal

Make the Turn Summary's Business costs breakdown reconcile to the committed
total when a business employs a Bookkeeper: today the tooltip's per-business
items use the card's raw `ongoingCost` while the engine charges the
Bookkeeper-reduced cost, so the difference is presented as a coin clamp.

Discovered from: `MS-0MWBZDVCH008P8X5` (per-card expense breakdowns on competitive Turn Summary seats).

## Evidence

- `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`) charges
  `effectiveBusinessOngoingCost(state, i, cost)` — the slot's own
  `computeBusinessOngoingCostReductionPct` (Bookkeeper, −20%) applied before the
  street-wide Cost Cutter reduction.
- `expenseLineBreakdown` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`) builds each
  business item from `(slot as BusinessCard).ongoingCost` with no per-business
  reduction, so `sum(items) + streetReduction` exceeds the committed line when a

- `buildExpenseLineTooltip` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts`)

  misleading: no clamp occurred.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Business expense breakdown items expose the Bookkeeper's per-business reduction as a named modifier (`base + sum(modifiers) === coins`), using `computeBusinessOngoingCostReductionPct` and the same helpers the engine charges with.
- The breakdown reconciles exactly to the committed business total for a state with an employed Bookkeeper, with no spurious clamp line in the tooltip.

## Goal

Align the single-player AI / Monte-Carlo hire path (Q3-A): a business-staff hire places the member at a legal destination business as part of the hire, or — when no legal destination exists — the hire is not taken, so an AI hire is never silently inert (the Delivery Driver hired and parked in the management company, wasting its salary).

Management-company staff hires stay as today (no destination).
- **Execution.** `executeAction` (`:1952` / `:2485`) handles the composite: hire the member and place it at the carried destination through the shared placement path, in the same turn/action.
